areas.rationale: Keep the provider-neutral API and its generated contracts in one removable product-owned boundary.
semantic_invariants: The API remains provider-neutral and cannot depend on TraceDecay host internals.
Generated contract bindings remain derived from the versioned provider contract set.

upstreamability.rationale: The provider-neutral contract can be proposed independently without carrying any concrete provider implementation.

areas.rationale: Keep routing, admission, and provider-neutral lifecycle behavior outside every concrete adapter and upstream host crate.
semantic_invariants: The fabric routes capabilities without branching on concrete provider names.
Unavailable providers remain typed failures and never trigger silent fallback.

upstreamability.rationale: The provider-neutral fabric is separable from product adapters and can converge through its public contracts.

areas.rationale: Own provider construction and activation outside the host while exposing one typed project-scoped composition object, the rank-final recall admission authority, and the application cognitive-recall port implementation the composition root mounts.
semantic_invariants: Disabled activation constructs no fabric, provider, storage, queue, or background worker.
Enabled Native activation requires the canonical application port explicitly.

Recall admission compares every candidate's seven exact-scope identity fields byte-for-byte against the scope the host dispatched; stale resolved-scope digests and unresolvable identities are distinct typed denials, never generic mismatches.

Validity windows, revocation, supersession, and unknown-validity policy are evaluated by the host after provider ordering and before any normalization or packing; denied candidates survive only as content-free ledger rows.
The recall bridge maps every non-success terminal and fabric error to a typed degradation or error and never reports an empty success.

upstreamability.rationale: Product selection and construction policy stays removable behind the narrow host composition mount.

areas.rationale: Adapt canonical Native application operations through one root-private application port while keeping its implementation and parity fixtures explicitly product-owned.
semantic_invariants: The adapter delegates all canonical effects through the injected Native application port.
Provider terminals cannot claim effects that the Native application port did not report.
Native recall is read-only, exact-scope bound, and semantically equal to the direct Native search after ADR-documented envelope normalization.

Native recall candidates carry validity instants as utc_rfc3339_nanos strings so the host admission authority can evaluate them; Native emits only current active-fact projections and never fabricates revocation or supersession.

A Native recall candidate's exact_scope_identity attests only the identity the fact record proves (its owner project); profile, repository, worktree, branch, session, and resolved-scope fields are emitted empty because the retained project store has no such dimension, so the host admission authority denies every Native candidate as unknown_identity with an audit row. Native recall stays scope-denied until fact scope is persisted at commit; the adapter never echoes the request scope onto a candidate.
The Native baseline runs the production adapter and application port over the provider-neutral scenario corpus and records measured terminals without fabricating admission.
tests: cargo test --profile bounded-test -p tracedecay --lib --features memory-provider-host native_recall_ -- --nocapture

upstreamability.rationale: The adapter remains product-owned while Native storage and application authority stay unchanged upstream.

upstreamability.rationale: The licensed external-provider adapter and its evidence remain isolated from the upstream host architecture.

areas.rationale: Keep black-box provider conformance, dummy-provider fixtures, and product host journeys in one observer-isolated test boundary.

Differential runs compare full identity, terminal, effect, and retained outcome semantics.
Baseline lanes are typed runner behaviors: the no-memory and explicit-documentation lanes never construct a MemoryProvider, and no lane falls back to another.

Every baseline report binds one shared-inputs digest over corpus, fixture, scope and recall catalogs, rubrics, contract set, and host configuration; reports with differing shared inputs are never comparable.
Baseline context cost is exact admitted bytes; token counts appear only under a pinned versioned estimator identity and are otherwise typed indeterminate.

upstreamability.rationale: Provider-neutral conformance behavior can be upstreamed independently from product provider implementations.

areas.rationale: Hold the versioned memory-quality, safety, cost, and latency metric catalog and its evaluator in one provider-neutral crate that consumes the conformance baseline report and never touches host, store, or adapter internals.

The aggregate task score, the safety gate, and the verdict are separate report fields; the verdict fails whenever any safety metric exceeds its ceiling or is indeterminate, any safety-critical rubric check is not a pass, or a terminal gate failed, regardless of the aggregate.
Unresolved candidate labels are never coerced to zero or to pass; label-based metrics report labeled, unlabeled, and indeterminate counts and become indeterminate when every candidate is unresolved.
Latency percentiles, token, curation, correction, and discovery values are typed indeterminate when the runner supplied no samples; nothing is fabricated and provider identity is metadata only.

upstreamability.rationale: Provider-neutral metric definitions and their evaluator can be upstreamed with the conformance harness independently from product provider implementations.

Delivery state, attempt history, and replay position survive process restart.
Retention expiry and privacy deletion purge observation content while leaving a digest-only audit trail.

upstreamability.rationale: The provider-neutral observation journal carries no provider implementation and can be proposed on its own once its delivery contract settles.

areas.rationale: Hold the one product-owned seam where the canonical observation store, the durable observation journal, the hygiene pipeline, and the provider registry meet, as a single file inside the retained-owner tree that the composition root mounts only under the optional host feature.

A withheld admission persists a typed reason and digests only, advances the replay cursor, and never creates delivery work; the canonical record is never rewritten or deleted.
Journalled payload bytes are the sanitized bytes and carry a sanitization binding whose receipt names exactly those bytes; delivery sends journal bytes verbatim.
Exact project and per-session scope is copied from the authoritative resolved scope and never re-derived from paths, CWD, or journal placement.

The delivery worker drives the journal's bounded retention sweep on an explicit cadence: expired rows are terminalized with a receipt before their content is purged, a backlog converges over worker turns, and a failed sweep is logged and waits out its backoff.
mount_and_replay is the single product-owned mount sequence the composition root calls: mount, authoritative startup replay, then the bounded live replay edge over the same registered store.

upstreamability.rationale: The journey composes product-owned journal and hygiene crates against the upstream store and Native application port; it is removable with the host feature and has no upstream counterpart to converge with.

Every admission report is retained in the project-owned SQLite ledger before the result is delivered; an unwritable ledger fails the recall with a typed audit error rather than delivering content whose denials are not audit-visible.

Ledger rows carry denial identities, typed reasons, and provider-claimed digests only; no table has a content column, and a replay of an identical report is idempotent while a divergent replay is a typed conflict.

On the production Native route a same-project fact committed from any checkout is denied per candidate by the host scope check (unknown_identity, because Native attests no worktree, branch, or session) and lands in the ledger; the application result carries no candidate content for it.

The mount holds the host-pinned ActiveRoutingPolicy and hands it to every session port unchanged; no port or provider can select a different provider than the one the routing gate named, and observer registrations are refused by routing before any handshake.

semantic_invariants: Disabled activation constructs no provider infrastructure or background work.

The daemon profile identity is threaded into the Native application port at mount (mount_project_memory_provider_host takes profile_identity.profile_id()); it is the only profile the Native adapter attests on a recall candidate, fixed at mount and never copied from a call's exact scope.

The journey mount receives every worker bound (journal retention, dispatch lease/batch/attempt budget/reap budget, park, sweep cadence) as one validated ObservationJourneyPolicyV1 from the composition root; a policy that cannot bound the worker refuses the mount with a typed error, and the composition root passes the product default rather than the journey minting limits.

exception.why_unavoidable: ConfigurationRegistry::core() is the only place a project setting can be declared with a scope, sensitivity, restart requirement, default, and a place in the transactional revision/rollback machinery. The application layer consumes an already-produced snapshot and the composition root reads settings rather than declaring them, so no product-owned crate can make these two settings exist.
alternatives_rejected: Read the memory settings from a product-owned side table instead of the registry
Fork the configuration registry into a product-owned crate
Hard-code the provider composition as always-on and drop the settings
Gate the provider on an environment variable or build feature only
